violations: The new component roundCorner division by 2.0 has no adjacent Java-source citation.

The new state shadowing branches that map true/yes to 3.0 and false/no to 0.0 have no adjacent Java-source citation. The account discusses conversion, but T14 rule 3 requires provenance beside each parity-affecting constant or branch.

findings: The durable account ca50f6d2e87b8cac1e0222f18b473406ffbbca06 is an ancestor of immutable implementation 60d16110082c189ba1f02ea3eb46a928a7f77cf2 and remains byte-unchanged. The PlantUML checkout exactly matches the account's Java revision, and the oracle JAR hash matches prior checker evidence.

All ten fresh sources are valid PlantUML diagrams. Their server-generated SVGs are well-formed, have expected CLASS or DESCRIPTION diagram types, contain no PlantUML error markers, and are byte-unique against every prior golden and perturbation source.

The parser does preserve final declaration order across theme execution: the theme-then-user component case ends with user colors, and the reversed user-then-theme case ends with Minty colors. The cross-family State.Arrow_Color compatibility alias also reaches the use-case renderer correctly.

The account's temporal invariant is not implemented. StyleDeclaration.source_line and epoch are retained, and StyleCascade.resolve_at exists, but no production caller uses resolve_at. Every adapter calls resolve(...), which is resolve_at(..., u64::MAX). Java Entity#getCurrentStyleBuilder returns the creation-time builder for pure CSS, switches all entities to the latest builder after any skinparam command, and Link#getStyleBuilder always returns the captured builder. The three temporal heldouts directly expose all three paths.

Class, component, and use-case adapters never add an entity stereotype to their StyleSignature. State is the only adapted family that calls with_stereotype. CSS-qualified class styles are therefore unreachable, and the legacy raw fallback compares stereotype strings only with eq_ignore_ascii_case rather than Java's dot/underscore cleaning. Both CSS and legacy stereotype counterexamples fail.

Sparse selector matching in StyleCascade is not sufficient when the adapter projects winners into a dense family struct with the wrong consumption order. In class rendering, class_style inherits root FontColor into attr_font_color; that field is consulted before the separately resolved header FontColor, so the less-specific root value defeats the header winner. Padding is also projected with incompatible geometry, and arrow FontColor is not projected into class relationship labels.

The component adapter consumes arrow LineColor and font properties but not arrow LineThickness or LineStyle, and does not project root/family padding. Both source-order controls therefore preserve final colors while losing Minty's line width and layout envelope.

The resolver's regular/dark map overlay mirrors the simple DarkString fallback rule statically: regular winners are retained and dark winners replace only matching properties. Product integration is incomplete because all four adapters hardcode StyleScheme::Regular and no reviewed path selects dark rendering. The dark heldout confirms normal rendering does not leak dark class colors but exposes missing root document background projection.
Mechanical anti-overfit searches are clean, but the constant-provenance gate is not: newly introduced /2.0 component corner conversion and 3.0/0.0 state shadow branches lack adjacent Java citations.
No Cargo, rustc, rustfmt, self-authored unit test, or production edit was used as checker evidence. The verdict rests on pinned-Java differential outputs plus static Java/Rust data-flow inspection.

Either expose and verify a product dark-scheme selection path or explicitly narrow the implementation claim; a resolver-only dark channel that no adapter can request is not product parity.
